commander.core: You see where things should go and help others commit to getting there.
commander.str: Long-range thinking · decisive calls · setting priorities · rallying people
commander.contrib: You give a team a “why” and a direction worth following.
commander.edge: Pair every vision with one concrete first step and one clear owner.
commander.watch: You may underestimate the detail and follow-through ideas need, or move on before they are executed.
commander.ally: A General to turn direction into results, and a Chancellor to make it sustainable.
commander.thrive: 1 → 10 growth stages: leading a team, function, venture or strategic initiative.

general.core: You turn goals into wins and move first when it matters.
general.str: Drive and ownership · urgency · resilience under pressure · closing
general.contrib: You create momentum and measurable results.
general.edge: Before charging, confirm the direction. After winning, capture what worked as a repeatable method.
general.watch: You may take on too much personally, skip systems, or burn out.
general.ally: A Commander to give you a battle worth winning, and a Chancellor to secure the gains.
general.thrive: 0 → 1 stages: frontline, sales, business development, launches, turnarounds.

chancellor.core: You make things run well, and you make them last.
chancellor.str: Process and governance · resource stewardship · risk awareness · reliability
chancellor.contrib: You create stability, so growth doesn’t collapse under its own weight.
chancellor.edge: Make your impact visible. Quantify the risk you prevented and the time you saved.
chancellor.watch: You may over-prepare, resist fast change, or go unnoticed because good systems are invisible.
chancellor.ally: A Commander to set direction, and a General to create momentum.
chancellor.thrive: 10 → 100 scale stages: operations, finance, HR, compliance, programme management, advisory.

GAP.commander: You may sometimes work hard on things that aren’t clearly moving you forward. Seek mentors or leaders with clear vision, and set your own 12-month direction.
GAP.general: Your ideas and systems may be ahead of your results. Work with doers, set short deadlines and celebrate small wins.
GAP.chancellor: You may create momentum faster than structure. Build simple systems, and partner with someone who loves stability and detail.

commander+general: You set the direction and lead the charge yourself.
commander+chancellor: You set the direction and build the structure to carry it.
general+chancellor: You deliver results and make them repeatable.

intro.headline: Last step: the role you'll play to get there.
intro.body: Every great team runs on three kinds of talent: the Commander 帅才 who sets direction, the General 将才 who delivers results, and the Chancellor 相才 who builds what lasts. Six quick scenarios. Choose what feels most like you.
intro.story:
Over 2,000 years ago, the founder of the Han dynasty explained his victory simply. He could not out-plan his strategist, out-govern his chancellor or out-fight his general. But he knew how to bring all three together. 吾能用之，此吾所以取天下也。

Today, every company, project and career still runs on the same Iron Triangle 铁三角.
